title: Which Discount a Pulled Catering Order Is Valued At
content:
## The rule

The trading discount taken on the value standing on a pulled order under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement is set by how often the agreement has actually been trading, measured by its delivery entries over the 6 months ending on the day notice is given.

1. **3 or more deliveries in the 6 months ending on the day notice is given** — the trading discount taken is the discount written onto the agreement.
2. **At least 1 but fewer than 3 deliveries in those 6 months** — the trading discount taken is the standing discount printed against the catering service level.
3. **No delivery in those 6 months** — no trading discount is taken.

## The two discounts are different records

The discount written onto the agreement is the figure recorded on that individual agreement. The standing discount printed against the catering service level is the schedule figure for that level. Where the two differ, the first branch gives the figure on the agreement and the second gives the figure from the schedule.

## Both sides of the counts

| Deliveries in the 6 months ending on the day notice is given | Trading discount taken |
| --- | --- |
| 5 | the discount written onto the agreement |
| 3 | the discount written onto the agreement |
| 2 | the standing discount printed against the service level |
| 1 | the standing discount printed against the service level |
| 0 | none |

On a hypothetical Attended Buffet Account whose agreement records a written discount of 4.0 per cent against a printed standing discount of 3.0 per cent: with 3 deliveries in that window the trading discount taken is 4.0 per cent; with 2 deliveries it is 3.0 per cent; with none it is nothing at all.
